    13  /-!
    14  # Monoid algebras
    15  
    16  When the domain of a `Finsupp` has a multiplicative or additive structure, we can define
    17  a convolution product. To mathematicians this structure is known as the "monoid algebra",
    18  i.e. the finite formal linear combinations over a given semiring of elements of a monoid `M`.
    19  The "group ring" `ℤ[G]` or the "group algebra" `k[G]` are typical uses.
    20  
    21  In fact the construction of the "monoid algebra" makes sense when `M` is not even a monoid, but
    22  merely a magma, i.e., when `M` carries a multiplication which is not required to satisfy any
    23  conditions at all. In this case the construction yields a not-necessarily-unital,
    24  not-necessarily-associative algebra but it is still adjoint to the forgetful functor from such
    25  algebras to magmas, and we prove this as `MonoidAlgebra.liftMagma`.
    26  
    27  In this file we define `MonoidAlgebra R M` and `AddMonoidAlgebra R M` as one-field structures around
    28  `M →₀ R`, and then define the convolution product on these.
    29  
    30  When the domain is additive, this is used to define polynomials:
    31  ```
    32  Polynomial R := AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ
    33  MvPolynomial σ α := AddMonoidAlgebra R (σ →₀ ℕ)
    34  ```
    35  
    36  When the domain is multiplicative, e.g. a group, this will be used to define the group ring.
    37  
    38  ## Notation
    39  
    40  We introduce the notation `R[M]` for both `MonoidAlgebra R M` and `AddMonoidAlgebra R M`.
    41  The notations are scoped to their respective namespaces, and which one `R[M]` resolves to therefore

    10  /-!
    11  # Type of functions with finite support
    12  
    13  For any type `α` and any type `M` with zero, we define the type `Finsupp α M` (notation: `α →₀ M`)
    14  of finitely supported functions from `α` to `M`, i.e. the functions which are zero everywhere
    15  on `α` except on a finite set.
    16  
    17  Functions with finite support are used (at least) in the following parts of the library:
    18  
    19  * `MonoidAlgebra R M` and `AddMonoidAlgebra R M` are defined as `M →₀ R`;
    20  
    21  * polynomials and multivariate polynomials are defined as `AddMonoidAlgebra`s, hence they use
    22    `Finsupp` under the hood;
    23  
    24  * the linear combination of a family of vectors `v i` with coefficients `f i` (as used, e.g., to
    25    define linearly independent family `LinearIndependent`) is defined as a map
    26    `Finsupp.linearCombination : (ι → M) → (ι →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M`.
    27  
    28  Some other constructions are naturally equivalent to `α →₀ M` with some `α` and `M` but are defined
    29  in a different way in the library:
    30  
    31  * `Multiset α ≃+ α →₀ ℕ`;
    32  * `FreeAbelianGroup α ≃+ α →₀ ℤ`.
    33  
    34  Most of the theory assumes that the range is a commutative additive monoid. This gives us the big
    35  sum operator as a powerful way to construct `Finsupp` elements, which is defined in
    36  `Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Finsupp/Basic.lean`.
    37  
    38  Many constructions based on `α →₀ M` are `def`s rather than `abbrev`s to avoid reusing unwanted type
    39  class instances. E.g., `MonoidAlgebra`, `AddMonoidAlgebra`, and types based on these two have
    40  non-pointwise multiplication.
    41  
    42  ## Main declarations
    43  
    44  * `Finsupp`: The type of finitely supported functions from `α` to `β`.
    45  * `Finsupp.onFinset`: The restriction of a function to a `Finset` as a `Finsupp`.
    46  * `Finsupp.mapRange`: Composition of a `ZeroHom` with a `Finsupp`.
    47  * `Finsupp.embDomain`: Maps the domain of a `Finsupp` by an embedding.
    48  * `Finsupp.zipWith`: Postcomposition of two `Finsupp`s with a function `f` such that `f 0 0 = 0`.
